# Active work — pdf-integrity

Live work, grouped by parent in `ROADMAP.md` order. Blocked work names its blocker inline.

## [M1 — factual audit utility](ROADMAP.md#m1--factual-audit-utility) `@audit.milestone.m1-factual-audit/1`

### Direct-edit provenance facts: touch-up markers and document lineage identifiers

`proposed` · `@audit.work.edit-provenance-facts/1` · part of `@audit.milestone.m1-factual-audit/1`

Two neutral fact families the M1 inventory currently omits, both cheap to reach and both decisive in the derived-document case.

First, an editing-marker inventory. Acrobat's interactive Edit Text tool wraps re-typed runs in marked content tagged /TouchUp_TextEdit (and related /TouchUp_* tags). Record every occurrence per page with its content-stream offset and the bounding box of the enclosed run. These tags are not emitted by print-to-PDF, Distiller from PostScript, OCR layers, or filing-portal conversion, so their presence — and especially their clustering around the regions that differ from a comparison document — is one of the few direct indicators of interactive text editing that survives in the file.

Second, document lineage identifiers as a first-class report section rather than loose XMP keys: xmpMM:DocumentID, xmpMM:InstanceID, xmpMM:OriginalDocumentID, xmpMM:DerivedFrom, the xmpMM:History event list, and both elements of the trailer /ID array. A save-as-and-edit cycle preserves DocumentID and trailer /ID[0] while minting a new InstanceID and /ID[1]; a genuine regeneration from the source application mints all of them fresh. Report these as facts and let the compare command and the findings engine interpret them.

Both are M1 fact-layer work under the pdf-read-facts / pdf-forensics-interpretation split. The marker inventory may need a neutral marked-content accessor surfaced from pdf-content, in which case that half becomes lege-namespace work.

## [M2 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m2-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m2-plan/1`

### pdf-source: bounded PrefixSource for revision replay

`proposed` · `@lege.work.prefix-source/1` · part of `@audit.work.m2-plan/1`

Add PrefixSource to pdf-source: a PdfSource wrapper exposing only bytes [0, end) of an underlying source, so any reliable logical-revision boundary can be opened through the ordinary DocumentSnapshot::open path and compiled, extracted and rendered with the existing machinery. No special historical-document implementation anywhere else.

### pdf-structure: preserve per-section xref entries

`proposed` · `@lege.work.xref-section-preservation/1` · part of `@audit.work.m2-plan/1`

Replace pdf-structure's two-field Revision (xref_offset, trailer) with the XrefSection model: offset, kind (Classic/Stream), preserved entry list, trailer, /Prev link, auxiliary_of for /XRefStm pairing, and per-section recovery events. The loader currently merges entries first-write-wins and discards which objects each section introduced; it must instead retain them (Arc slices, materialized only on the audit path) while leaving the fast rendering path's behavior and performance unchanged. This is the single load-bearing lege-pdf refactor for the checker — everything in M2 and M3 rests on it.

## [M3 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m3-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m3-plan/1`

### pdf-document: forensic identity fields on PageAnnotation

`proposed` · `@lege.work.annotation-forensic-metadata/1` · part of `@audit.work.m3-plan/1`

PageAnnotation preserves rendering fields but not annotation object identity or provenance. Add the neutral facts the overlay analyzer needs: source ObjectId, /Contents, /NM unique name, /M modified date, /CreationDate, /T author, /Subj subject, /IT intent. These are facts, not findings — they belong in the document model, and the forensic interpretation stays in pdf-forensics per the crate-shape decision.

### pdf-content: optional PageTrace op-provenance sidecar

`proposed` · `@lege.work.page-trace-sidecar/1` · part of `@audit.work.m3-plan/1`

An audit-mode-only compile trace parallel to SemanticPage::ops: for each operator, the source stream object, nested object stack (form XObjects, patterns, Type 3), byte span within the stream, operator index, and PaintOrigin. The existing attribution map ignores alpha, blend modes and soft masks and records only broad origin categories, so it generates occlusion candidates but cannot serve as final evidence; PageTrace closes that gap without widening any normal render path — it is produced only when the audit flag asks for it.

## Unparented

### Two-file compare mode (suspect vs trusted original)

`proposed` · `@audit.work.compare-command/1`

A `compare suspect.pdf trusted-original.pdf` command. A trusted original changes the problem class entirely: coherent full rewrites and rasterized replacements become directly detectable instead of merely anomalous. Compare at the same three levels as revision diff — object inventory, semantic text/font/image, deterministic visual — and report per-page divergence with evidence artifacts. Reuses the whole M3 diff engine; the new work is input pairing, page correspondence (documents may differ in page count), and a report section that distinguishes 'derived from the original' from 'unrelated document'.

### Heuristic: font-resource fragmentation within a single text run

`proposed` · `@audit.work.intra-run-font-fragmentation/1`

Detect the case where a contiguous visible text run is drawn from more than one font resource, and the minority resource covers only the characters that carry the semantic change — for example a date where the two altered digits use one font resource while the surrounding digits and the separator stay in the original.

The mechanism is specific: when text is re-typed in place, the glyphs needed for the new characters are often absent from the original embedded subset, so the editor emits a second font resource — typically a fresh subset with very small glyph coverage, or a non-embedded substitute — for just those glyphs. A document regenerated from its source application draws the whole run from one resource. The signal is therefore strongest when the minority resource's glyph coverage is tiny and its subset tag differs from the majority resource's while the underlying base font name matches.

Report as a bounded finding with the run's text, the two resources, their subset tags and glyph coverage, and the page location. Legitimate producers do split runs across resources — script and symbol fallback, mixed-language text, and some form-field flattening all do it — so this must be validated against the legitimate-producer corpus before it can carry weight, and it should never be a standalone basis for a suspicion finding.

### M1 plan of record

`proposed` · `@audit.work.m1-plan/1`

Order of work: (1) define the AuditReport JSON schema and Finding/EvidenceStrength types in the new pdf-forensics crate; (2) extend pdf-read's existing doctor output with the missing inventories (annotation identity fields, signature dictionaries and ByteRange, per-page representation metrics from SemImage/SemFont counts, image coverage and effective DPI); (3) implement the PageRepresentation classifier over prepare_rgb_image_page and the semantic page; (4) wire a `pdf-cli audit` subcommand emitting JSON and terminal output; (5) build the ten M1 acceptance fixtures in pdf-test-support plus real captured producer outputs. No new parsing work is required for M1 — it is assembly and classification over facts pdf-read already reaches.

### M4 plan of record

`proposed` · `@audit.work.m4-plan/1`

Order of work: (1) structural layer — /FT /Sig discovery, signature dictionary parsing, strict ByteRange shape/order/bounds validation against raw bytes, revision association, post-signature object-change lists; (2) DocMDP and FieldMDP policy parsing and compliance evaluation; (3) crypto layer behind the crate chosen by the open crypto-crate question — CMS/CAdES digest verification first, then certificate chain, trust and timestamp reporting. The structural layer must not depend on the crypto layer compiling: layer one ships even if the crate decision slips.

### M5 plan of record

`proposed` · `@audit.work.m5-plan/1`

Order of work, gated on the M1-M4 utility already proving useful: (1) stand up the corpus-sweep harness and false-positive measurement over the legitimate corpus before writing any heuristic; (2) font-layer heuristics (font-program hashes, per-line font-identity outliers, subset glyph-coverage anomalies) — SemFont already preserves everything needed, no OCR; (3) text-layout heuristics (spacing, matrix, TJ-style outliers); (4) serialization heuristics (stream filters, object-number and resource-name clusters); (5) metadata timeline checks; (6) image-statistics outliers (DPI, codec, quantization, colorspace); (7) producer fingerprints, as corroboration only, never primary evidence. Each heuristic lands with its measured per-producer false-positive rate or it does not land.

### OCR cross-check layer (lege-ocr)

`proposed` · `@audit.work.ocr-crosscheck/1`

Optional OCR-backed checks for raster and mixed pages, using the existing lege-ocr crate rather than a new dependency: (1) compare a page image against its invisible OCR text layer and flag hidden-vs-visible disagreement; (2) read a raster patch placed over vector content and compare its text against the prior revision's text at that rectangle; (3) baseline and typeface anomaly hints in raster-only documents. Ships as a feature-gated module so the core checker keeps its no-OCR dependency footprint; findings emit at ContextualIndicator strength or below.
